exposure: timing of prophylactic antibiotics (after cord clamping)
outcome: prevalence of postoperative infection (endometritis, surgical-site infection, sepsis)
other infections (mastitis, urinary tract infection, pneumonia)
cohort: 2,725 women giving birth by non-elective cesarean section between 2010 and 2017 at a single labor ward in Denmark.
finding: The prevalence of main composite infections (endometritis, surgical-site infection, or sepsis) was 3.2%, which is considered low, suggesting that administering prophylactic antibiotics after cord clamping is an acceptable practice.
